easy.q: In Elder Bednar’s story, why was the man not allowed to enter the country he was visiting?
options: He had left his passport at home
His passport was damaged and badly repaired
He arrived on the wrong day
easy.why: The man had a valid passport, but he “had not taken good care” of it. It was stained, torn, and fixed with tape and glue, so the official would not stamp it.

easy.q: Elder Bednar shared President Packer’s teaching that life is a journey for all of us. Where does that journey lead?
options: Home, back to the presence of God
Around the whole wide world
To a place nobody can know about
easy.why: President Packer taught that “life is a homeward journey for all of us, back to the presence of God.”

easy.q: According to Elder Bednar, what is a covenant?
options: A wish we hope will come true someday
A rule we make up for ourselves
A solemn promise between God and His children
easy.why: Elder Bednar said a covenant is “a solemn promise,” a lasting commitment between God and His sons and daughters.

easy.q: Elder Bednar taught that the Holy Ghost is a messenger. Whose messenger is He?
options: The angels in heaven
The prophets of old
The Father and the Son
easy.why: Elder Bednar said the Holy Ghost “testifies of all truth, and is the witness of and messenger for the Father and the Son.”

easy.q: At the end of his talk, Elder Bednar shared King Benjamin’s promise. What happens to those who keep God’s commandments faithfully to the end?
options: They dwell with God in never-ending happiness
They never have any hard days again
They become rich and well known
easy.why: King Benjamin taught that the faithful are “received into heaven” to live with God “in a state of never-ending happiness.”

medium.q: What did Elder Bednar say is the simple lesson of the passport story?
options: Travelers should plan carefully before a long journey
Border officials decide who is worthy to enter
A passport is useful only if family is waiting
A passport must be kept whole over time, not just held
medium.why: He taught that “the integrity of a passport must be maintained over time.” Holding one gave the man a chance to enter, but it did not guarantee he would.

medium.q: Elder Bednar compared the stamp the man needed in his passport to something each of us needs. What is it?
options: A current temple recommend
The verifying witness of the Holy Spirit of Promise
A blessing from a priesthood leader
A record of our baptism and confirmation
medium.why: Just as the man needed an authorized stamp, each of us needs “the verifying witness of the Holy Spirit of Promise” to receive the eternal blessings of our covenants.

medium.q: Elder Bednar said his passport analogy “has limitations.” What limitation did he point out?
options: Trials that are not our fault do not invalidate our covenants
Covenants, unlike passports, can never be harmed by our choices
A lost passport can be replaced, but a covenant cannot be renewed
Passports matter in this life, but covenants matter only in the next
medium.why: Unlike damage to a passport, “the adversities and afflictions we experience through no fault of our own” do not diminish God’s promises or invalidate our covenants.

medium.q: According to Elder Bednar, how does the ratifying sealing by the Holy Ghost typically come?
options: All at once, when an ordinance is performed
Only after this life, at the Final Judgment
Over time, as we repent and honor our covenants
Once, when we first feel the Spirit strongly
medium.why: He said it “typically is not a one-time event”; it comes over time as we repent sincerely and consistently, honor our covenants, and yield our hearts to God.

medium.q: Elder Bednar said a faithful spouse may ask whether another person’s unrighteous choices can rob them of what God has promised. How did he answer?
options: Yes, until the other person chooses to repent fully
No; another’s unrighteousness cannot block God’s blessings
Only the blessings of this life can be taken away
He said the question cannot be answered in this life
medium.why: He said the answer is “an emphatic no!” Another person’s unrighteous use of moral agency cannot rob a faithful spouse of what God has promised.

hard.q: Elder Bednar described two parts of the sealing ordinance, a “lateral” and a “vertical” sealing. Which pairing matches what he taught?
options: Lateral: the couple sealed into God’s eternal family; vertical: husband and wife in marriage
Lateral: parents sealed to their children; vertical: husband and wife united in marriage
Lateral: the sealing made on earth; vertical: its ratifying by the Holy Spirit of Promise
Lateral: husband and wife in marriage; vertical: the couple sealed into God’s eternal family
hard.why: The lateral sealing is “the eternal union of a man and a woman in marriage.” The vertical sealing joins husband and wife to “God’s eternal family” and links humankind through all generations. He said both are vital.

hard.q: Which statement matches what Elder Bednar taught about the sealing by the Holy Spirit of Promise during mortality?
options: It is conditional and can be forfeited through unrighteousness
It is permanent once given, whatever we choose afterward
It can be lost through hardships that are not our fault
It is never given until mortal life is over
hard.why: A covenant sealed by the Holy Spirit of Promise is binding on earth and in heaven, yet “this sealing is conditional in mortality” and can be broken or forfeited through unrighteousness.

hard.q: When a temple marriage does not endure, what did Elder Bednar say a faithful, covenant-keeping spouse remains worthy to receive?
options: No ratifying seal for either aspect until the other spouse has fully repented
The ratifying seal for both the lateral and vertical aspects, just as before
The ratifying seal for the lateral aspect only, with the vertical held in reserve
The ratifying seal for the vertical aspect, with all associated individual blessings
hard.why: A faithful spouse “remains worthy to receive for himself or herself” the ratifying seal for the vertical aspect of the sealing ordinance and all other associated individual blessings.

hard.q: Speaking of faithful members whose temple marriage does not endure, what did Elder Bednar say he does not know, and what did he say he does know?
options: He does not know why trials come, but knows they will end soon
He does not know how or when blessings come, but knows they will come
He does not know who will be faithful, but knows who will be blessed
He does not know which blessings are promised, but knows God is fair
hard.why: He said, “I do not know and cannot explain precisely how and when promised blessings are received. But I do know promised blessings will be received.”

hard.q: Which situation best fits the warning in Elder Bednar’s passport parable about spiritual credentials?
options: A covenant keeper who suffers a serious illness through no fault of their own
A person learning about the gospel who has not yet been baptized
A person baptized long ago who has stopped keeping covenants but relies on the ordinance
A person who repents often and keeps striving to honor covenants
hard.why: The man held a valid passport but had not cared for it. Elder Bednar taught, “Ongoing faithfulness is required for those credentials to be valid and for promised blessings to be received.”
